comments.author: _Suomi
comments.body_html:
Yep, it’s exactly that: real long-range VOIP radio comms, ACRE/TFAR-style, not canned F1/F2 voice lines.

It hooks into the actual Dissonance voice chat (the same system EFT/Fika use for proximity VOIP) and opens a separate radio channel on top of it. Range is extended way past normal proximity chat, with per-radio signal degradation as distance increases (static, robotic/digital distortion, dropouts) every radio has its own distinct “voice”/DSP character and max range, so a cheap Baofeng sounds and reaches very differently than something like the Harris AN/PRC-152.

No pre-recorded lines involved anywhere - it’s your actual live voice, same as normal proximity chat, just routed through the radio channel with distance-based effects applied in real time.

comments.body_html: Thanks for the mod, works well on headless Fika. One question: the item marks itself as SPEC, but we can’t put it into SPEC slot. Is this intended?

comments.author: _Suomi
comments.body_html:
Thanks, glad it’s working well on headless!

That’s intentional, not a bug — radios can’t go in the SPEC slot (and can’t be insured either) on purpose. The idea is to add a bit of stakes to holding onto them: if you lose your gear in a raid, you actually lose the radio too, rather than it being a free, risk-free item like insured SPEC slot gear usually is. Encourages actually protecting/keeping track of them instead of treating them as disposable.

That said, I’m open to revisiting this down the line — if enough people feel it’s too punishing or doesn’t fit how they play, I might look into some middle ground. Feedback on this specific point is welcome, feel free to weigh in.

comments.author: _Suomi
comments.body_html: It’s marked as SPEC because functionally it’s in the same category as the multitool, compass, and rangefinder — that’s why it inherited that slot’s item type/behavior.

comments.author: makshepard
comments.body_html:
Hello! The mod works if you launch a solo raid. There’s an indicator in the bottom right corner, as has been noted, but a single gray dot means the radio is inactive.

Put the radio in your rig, try turning it on (Ctrl + “K” or your VOIP keybind), and a notification should appear in the bottom right corner indicating that it’s enabled.

If that doesn’t happen, here are some basic troubleshooting suggestions:

  1. Check that the Fika mod is installed (without it, the mod’s functionality is not guaranteed).
  2. Verify that the PRT mod itself is installed correctly (sometimes the archive gets extracted improperly — it never hurts to double-check).
  3. In the game itself, check the PRT mod settings and make sure notifications are enabled (in the F12 settings overlay, under the PRT mod section, there is a specific option for this).

If all of the above checks out, you have the radio with you in the raid, and the notifications still don’t appear, then write back here again and we’ll try to figure it out in more detail together.

comments.author: _Suomi
comments.body_html:
Haha, appreciate it! Answering both:

  1. There’s no separate language toggle for it - the on-screen notification text (and the F12-menu-adjacent overlay) automatically follows whatever language your actual game client is set to (Settings → Language in EFT itself), not a config option in the mod. Good catch though - I hadn’t accounted for anything besides English/Russian, so any other language was silently falling back to Russian, which obviously wasn’t great. Just flipped that: now Russian only shows if you’ve actually got Russian selected, everyone else defaults to English going forward.

  2. Ha, that’s actually a fun idea - piping the vanilla quick-voiceline wheel (F1/F2/etc.) through the radio channel so it reaches AI teammates over PTT. Right now the mod only carries real live VOIP audio through the radio, nothing hooks into the quick-voiceline system at all. Not something planned for the near term (it’s a genuinely different integration point - quick-lines are their own separate system from the Dissonance voice chat this mod taps into), but it’s a neat idea for down the line. Thanks for tossing it out there, not mad at all o7
